gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 300 sold with the same 2× 200 W panels gave 2,650 Wh in Notebookcheck's discharge test and 2,819 Wh in The Technology Man's. That is about 55–65% more usable AC energy than the 1,710 Wh OutdoorGearLab measured from the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2, the 400 W kit ChatGPT and PowerSized lean on, and the Elite 300 kit costs $1,614.05 through our link. One catch: the Elite 300 kit is a pre-order that the store says dispatches in late November 2026.
standout_why: StormWatts (the cited page, 2026-11-08/12) has no measurements at all and says 'We have not tested these products hands-on'. Its refill figures use an assumed 0.85 efficiency. Trek4Tech says 'We did not test any of these units'. OutageReady says 'We haven't tested these bundles hands-on' and uses a 0.7 derate. PowerSized has only two measured figures, both from OutdoorGearLab: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at 1,710 Wh and AC180 at 950 Wh. Our own page (dealectric.com/solar-generator-with-panels-included) adds StorageReview's 1.91 kWh for the Elite 200 V2, plus OGL figures for the DELTA 3, C1000 Gen 2 and panels. None of these pages gives a measured figure for the Elite 300, Elite 400 or ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro. None puts the 400 W kits side by side by measured usable energy, and none has a measured figure for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max that ChatGPT picked.
decides: Price per measured Wh changes the ranking of the 400 W kits. At the link price, the Elite 400 + 2×200 W comes to about $0.59/Wh (StorageReview US unit) and the Elite 300 + 2×200 W to about $0.57–0.61/Wh. The Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W, ChatGPT's pick, comes to about $0.75/Wh, and the AC180 + 2×200 W to about $1.23/Wh. Both Elite 300/400 kits are pre-orders: the Elite 300 dispatches late November and the Elite 400 mid-December, so they belong in the 'if you can wait' slot. The measurements also argue against our ships-now ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SP037 400 W kit ($917.93). StorageReview measured only 920 Wh from the S2000 Pro, which shut off at 22%, and said it uses older NCM cells. That was a 2023 test of a unit with a 1,500 Wh claim, so treat it as a warning, not a verdict. No lab figure was found for the other ships-now ALLPOWERS 400 W kits (R2500 V2, R3500), so the ships-now pick has to rest on specs, not measurements. ChatGPT's EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max has no published measurement. The nearest is the DELTA 3 Max Plus, a different model, which gave 1,898 Wh.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: about 2,650 Wh of 3,014.4 Wh rated (just under 88%)
findings.source_title: 3 kWh in a compact package: Powerstation Bluetti Elite 300 review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, published 2026-03-09, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Steady load of just over 200 W. Notebookcheck says efficiency rose to 'just over 92 percent' at 1,800 W but gives no Wh figure for that load. It tested the EU version, which it says differs slightly from the US version. AC charging: 3,450 Wh drawn from the wall to fill the battery, about 87% reaching it. Fan noise over 50 dB at 1 m under load. Price per measured Wh: $1,614.05 link price ÷ 2,650 Wh = $0.609/Wh.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy and solar input (The Technology Man)
findings.value: 2,819 Wh of 3,014 Wh rated (93.5%); about 550 W solar from 750 W of panels
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 300 Review – 3kWh Capacity – But There Are Compromises (The Technology Man, Gidon, 2026-03-25)
findings.note: Constant 1 kW resistive heater load: ran 2 h 46 min. Solar: about 250 W from one BLUETTI PV350. About 550 W at about 31 V (just under 18 A) with the PV350 plus two Renogy 200 W panels in parallel. Not the kit's own 2× 200 W panels. Price per measured Wh: $1,614.05 ÷ 2,819 = $0.573/Wh.

findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 review (OutdoorGearLab, Chris McNamara with Kenji Mowrey, 2025-11-03)

findings.label: Measured discharge (StorageReview)
findings.value: 920 Wh at a 350 W load; unit shut off with 22% showing; claim was 1,500 Wh
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro Portable Power Station Review (StorageReview Consumer Desk, 2023-04-07)
findings.note: StorageReview says the unit uses older NCM (ternary) cells, not LiFePO4, and reports battery-calibration problems. The tested unit was listed at 1,500 Wh, but the kit we link lists 1,451 Wh, so it is not established that this is the same hardware. Use as a caution, not a current rating. Against today's 1,451 Wh listing: 920 ÷ 1,451 = 63%. Price per measured Wh for the S2000 Pro + SP037 kit: $917.93 link price ÷ 920 Wh = $0.998/Wh.
